title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Every effect, and every option, rendered."
description: "The complete Animate.css effect gallery played by the extension, alongside worked examples of the timing options."
---

Everything below is rendered by the extension as this page is built.
The site sets `duration: 1s` and `delay: 1s`, rather than the extension's own `3s` and `2s`, so the gallery plays without a long wait.
Every other option is left at its default.

Animations play once, as the page loads.
Reload to watch them again.

::: {.callout-important}
A reader whose system asks for reduced motion sees no animation on this page, and printed output carries none either.
The bundled stylesheet answers `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and `print` by cutting every animation to `1ms` and a single run, with `!important`, which beats the inline duration the shortcode writes.
The same block sets `opacity: 0` on any element whose class list contains `Out`, so every exit effect is hidden outright rather than played.

It does not touch `animation-delay`.
A delayed entrance therefore still waits, and holds its first frame while it waits, so the text on this page that carries `delay=3s` stays invisible for three seconds and then appears at once.
Use `delay` sparingly for that reason.
:::

## Timing

`duration` is written as an inline style, so any CSS time works exactly.

| Source | Renders as |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< animate pulse "Quick" duration=500ms >}}}` | {{< animate pulse "Quick" duration=500ms >}} |
| `{{{< animate pulse "Slow" duration=4s >}}}` | {{< animate pulse "Slow" duration=4s >}} |

: The same effect at two durations. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[60,40]"}

`repeat` maps to an Animate.css class, and only `1`, `2`, `3`, and `infinite` have one.

| Source | Renders as |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< animate tada "Three times" repeat=3 >}}}` | {{< animate tada "Three times" repeat=3 >}} |
| `{{{< animate heartBeat "Forever" repeat=infinite >}}}` | {{< animate heartBeat "Forever" repeat=infinite >}} |

: Repeating an animation. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[60,40]"}

`direction` reverses or alternates the animation, and is most visible when it repeats.

| Source | Renders as |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< animate bounce "Reverse" direction=reverse repeat=2 >}}}` | {{< animate bounce "Reverse" direction=reverse repeat=2 >}} |
| `{{{< animate bounce "Alternate" direction=alternate repeat=2 >}}}` | {{< animate bounce "Alternate" direction=alternate repeat=2 >}} |

: Playing an animation backwards. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[60,40]"}

`delay` maps to an Animate.css class as well, and only whole seconds from `1s` to `5s` have one.

| Source | Renders as |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< animate fadeIn "After three seconds" delay=3s >}}}` | {{< animate fadeIn "After three seconds" delay=3s >}} |
| `{{{< animate fadeIn "Straight away" delay=500ms >}}}` | {{< animate fadeIn "Straight away" delay=500ms >}} |

: A delay that reaches the output, and one that does not. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[60,40]"}

The second call is valid, and it writes the class `animate__delay-500ms`, which no rule matches.
That text therefore animates at once.
The class multiplies `--animate-delay` rather than setting an absolute time, and the extension writes that variable once per document.
On this page it holds `1s`, so `animate__delay-3s` is three seconds here.
See [What the timing values actually do](reference.qmd#what-the-timing-values-actually-do) for the full rule.

## Sequencing

`stagger` adds an increment to the delay of each successive shortcode, so a run of them arrives in order rather than together.

```markdown
{{{< animate fadeIn "One" stagger=1s >}}}
{{{< animate fadeIn "Two" stagger=1s >}}}
{{{< animate fadeIn "Three" stagger=1s >}}}
```

{{< animate fadeIn "One" stagger=1s >}}
{{< animate fadeIn "Two" stagger=1s >}}
{{< animate fadeIn "Three" stagger=1s >}}

::: {.callout-note}
The increment is applied as a delay, so it is subject to the same limitation: only whole seconds from one to five reach the output.
An increment of `300ms` validates and then does nothing.
:::

## Setting the options once

Every attribute is also an option under `extensions.animate`, in the front matter of a document or in a project's `_quarto.yml`.
This site sets two of them:

```yaml
extensions:
  animate:
    duration: 1s
    delay: 1s
```

An attribute on a call beats that block, and the block beats the extension's own defaults of `3s` and `2s`.

| Source | Renders as |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< animate rotateIn "Project setting" >}}}` | {{< animate rotateIn "Project setting" >}} |
| `{{{< animate rotateIn "Call setting" duration=5s >}}}` | {{< animate rotateIn "Call setting" duration=5s >}} |

: The project value, and a call that overrides it. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[60,40]"}

The first turns for one second, from the block above.
The second turns for five.
See [Options](reference.qmd#options) for the full list.

::: {.callout-caution}
The block must sit under `extensions`.
A top-level `animate:` block is ignored, which leaves the defaults in place.
It warns as well when it holds `duration`, `delay` or `repeat`, and says nothing when it holds only `stagger` or `direction`.
See [Validation](reference.qmd#validation).
:::

## Quoting the text

The text is the second positional argument, so it needs quotes as soon as it contains a space.

Without quotes, each word becomes a separate argument.
The shortcode reads the first two, warns about the rest, and animates one word only:

```markdown
{{{< animate bounce Two words >}}}
```

That call writes `Two` and drops `words` from the page.
The extension warns that it received three arguments where two are defined, and that the extras were ignored.
This page does not render the call, because the site is built with no warnings.

A double quote cannot be typed inside double-quoted text.
A backslash does not escape it: the text is cut at the backslash, and the call warns.

Quote the argument with apostrophes instead, and the double quotes pass through:

```markdown
{{{< animate bounce 'She said "go"' >}}}
```

{{< animate bounce 'She said "go"' >}}

The HTML entity works as well, and is the way to carry both kinds of quote at once:

```markdown
{{{< animate bounce "She said &quot;go&quot;" >}}}
```

{{< animate bounce "She said &quot;go&quot;" >}}

An apostrophe needs no entity:

```markdown
{{{< animate bounce "It's fine" >}}}
```

{{< animate bounce "It's fine" >}}

See [Shortcode](reference.qmd#shortcode) for both arguments.

## Special characters

The text is HTML-escaped, so punctuation that would otherwise break the markup survives:

```markdown
{{{< animate bounce "Cats & dogs <3" >}}}
```

{{< animate bounce "Cats & dogs <3" >}}

## Animating something other than plain text

The shortcode's second argument is plain text, so markdown inside it is not parsed.
This does not produce a link:

```markdown
{{{< animate bounce "[Animate.css](https://animate.style)" >}}}
```

Write the Animate.css classes on a span instead, which leaves the markdown to Quarto:

```markdown
[[Animate.css](https://animate.style)]{.animate__animated .animate__bounce style="display:inline-block;"}
```

[[Animate.css](https://animate.style)]{.animate__animated .animate__bounce style="display:inline-block;"}

Or on a div, for a whole block:

```markdown
::: {.animate__animated .animate__bounce}
[Animate.css](https://animate.style)
:::
```

::: {.animate__animated .animate__bounce}
[Animate.css](https://animate.style)
:::

A hand-written element carries no inline duration, so it takes `--animate-duration` instead.
The extension writes that variable once per document, from the first `animate` shortcode in it.
On this page that call is the `duration=500ms` one under [Timing](#timing), so the span and the div above both run in half a second rather than the project's one second.

## Effects

Every effect the extension accepts, played by the extension.

Animate.css keeps the last frame of an animation, so each exit effect below leaves its text invisible, or moved out of place, once it has played.

## Reveal.js

In `html` an animation plays once, when the page loads.
Under `revealjs` the extension also loads `animate.js`, which listens for `slidechanged` and replays the effect each time the slide comes into view.

This site is an `html` site, so the deck below is source only:

```markdown
---
format: revealjs
---

## A slide

{{{< animate bounce "Plays on every visit to this slide" >}}}
```

See [Output](reference.qmd#output) for what each format loads.
